items.question: Which organ pumps blood around your body?
items.explanation: The heart is a strong muscle that pumps blood all day and night. Blood carries oxygen and food to every part of the body. Your heart is about the size of your fist.

items.question: An adult human body has 206 bones.
items.explanation: Adults have 206 bones. Babies are born with more, but some of them join together as the child grows. The smallest bone is in the ear.
items.funFact: More than half of your bones are in your hands and feet.

items.question: Which organs clean the blood and make urine?
items.explanation: The two kidneys filter waste and extra water out of the blood. This waste leaves the body as urine. Each kidney is about the size of a closed fist.

items.fact: Red blood cells carry oxygen from your lungs to every part of your body.
items.explanation: They contain haemoglobin, a protein that holds oxygen and gives blood its red colour. Your body makes millions of new red blood cells every second.

items.question: In which part of the body is most digested food absorbed into the blood?
items.explanation: The small intestine is a long, coiled tube. Its inner wall has tiny finger-like parts called villi, which give it a huge surface to absorb food. The large intestine mainly absorbs water.
